Hi Olivia / Marcus —

Thanks for the call earlier. This thread is a quick post-call recap + the operational "gradebook" we discussed (what success looks like, how we'll measure it, who owns each piece, and the immediate milestones). Please confirm anything I missed.

TL;DR agreed success criteria (prep for POC):
- 99th percentile per-request latency under 800ms for typical prompt length (500 tokens) during sustained 50 RPS.
- End-to-end token throughput capacity to sustain 150K tokens/min for peak ingestion windows.
- Error rate below 0.5% (5xx / timeouts) across a 24-hour soak.
- No more than 5% degradation in output quality on our canonical eval set vs baseline (you provided baseline last week).

Evaluation plan (high level):
1) Week 0 (this week): confirm workload matrix + mutual action plan attached.
2) Week 1: instrument test harness and telemetry; initial throughput probe at low concurrency (10 RPS).
3) Week 2: ramp to sustained target (50 RPS) and run 24-hour soak; run quality evals at 10k sample points.
4) Week 3: burst testing (1-minute bursts to 200 RPS) and canary handoff for your staging traffic.

Workload profile (from today's notes) — please correct if different:
- Typical request rate: 10–50 RPS (target sustained = 50 RPS).
- Concurrency per session: 1–4 active requests (typical chat clients spawn 1.8 avg).
- Median prompt length: 120 tokens; mean response length: 380 tokens; 95th percentile combined tokens: ~1100.
- Burst pattern: daily peak at 10:00–11:00 PST with short multi-minute bursts up to ~200 RPS (usually lasting 60–120s).

Owners / immediate next steps: (owners in parentheses)
- Confirm workload matrix + baseline samples (Olivia) — due EOD Thu 8-Apr.
- Redwoods: telemetry spec + test harness access (Jordan) — draft by Fri 9-Apr.
- Schedule canary window & test IP whitelists (Ben) — coordinate with your infra team, target Mon 12-Apr.

Attachments in this message: redwood_poc_operational_gradebook_v1.pdf (operational checks + measurement definitions), mutual-action-plan_CLSPR.xlsx, traffic_matrix_v1.csv.

Please reply with any corrections to the workload profile or the timeline. Once Olivia confirms baseline samples, we'll schedule the initial probe and send the telemetry endpoints.

Thanks,
Naomi

Thanks for the concise recap, and yes this mirrors our internal notes. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- Baseline evaluation set: we'll share the 500-sample baseline and the automated scoring rubric by EOD Thursday (attached as a link in the Drive). Expect a representative mix across our three top intents.
- Burst distribution: our peak bursts are sometimes double-peaked inside the hour (i.e., two 30–45s spikes inside the 10:00 hour). Please plan for that pattern for the canary.
- Latency budget: 99th <800ms for the request path is acceptable, but we need a soft-failure mode if latency drifts above 1s (fall back to smaller model variant). Is that something Redwood's router can do automatically?

On owners: Olivia will drop baseline by EOD Thu 8-Apr. Marcus will introduce our infra lead (Matteo) on Friday to start IP whitelisting.

2) Test harness access: I'll provision a sandbox API key (role-limited) and a short README for their infra team to push sample traffic. Expect an access email from infra@redwood.ai by Fri 9-Apr 11:00 PDT.
3) Canary policy: automatic model-fallback threshold is configurable; we can set a 1s 99th threshold to swap to the quantized 1.3B variant and record output-delta metrics. We'll propose the exact rule in the mutual action plan.

- Please mark which endpoints in your sample set are latency-sensitive vs. throughput-sensitive (add a column to the traffic_matrix_v1.csv).
- Confirm whether the 24-hour soak should include daytime business hours only or a rolling 24-hour window (our default is rolling 24-hour).
